title: Condition Monitoring Records Missing After a Rotation — Fault Symptom

issue.reason: Original issue of the fault symptom procedure for missing condition monitoring records.

abstract: Symptom-driven isolation of missing condition monitoring records, separating store overwriting because collection was late from a genuine recording or interface fault.

sections.purpose: This procedure isolates the cause of condition monitoring records that are missing from the operator's ground system after a rotation, and identifies whether the records were ever written.
sections.fault_description: The engineering team reports a gap in the condition monitoring record sequence for one or more sectors, usually after an aircraft has been away from base for several days. Nothing is indicated on the aircraft. The most common cause is not a recording fault at all: the on-board store has filled and overwritten the oldest closed records before anyone connected to collect them. A genuine recording fault shows a gap that is not aligned with the store capacity.
sections.isolation_procedure: 1. Read the store fill level and the timestamp of the oldest retained record from the data server module. 2. Calculate the retention achieved in days and compare it with the elapsed time since the last successful collection. 3. If the missing records are older than the retention achieved, the store has overwritten them and no fault exists on the aircraft. 4. In that case record the shortfall and raise the collection interval or the store capacity with the operator's engineering department. 5. If the missing records are inside the retention window, read the record sequence numbers and identify whether the gap is contiguous. 6. A contiguous gap that starts at a power cycle points at an interrupted write rather than at a failed collection. 7. Check the maintenance interface unit for reported write errors and read its fault log. 8. Run the built-in test load and record the result. 9. If the built-in test fails, replace the data server module and repeat the store integrity check. 10. If the built-in test passes and the gap persists on the next rotation, replace the maintenance interface unit.
sections.dispatch_note: There is no dispatch consequence. The condition monitoring function is not required for dispatch and no minimum equipment list item applies, but a persistent recording fault should be cleared before the aircraft next leaves its main base.

possible_causes.cause: On-board store overwritten because collection was later than the retention achieved

title: Condition Monitoring Records Missing After a Rotation — Fault Symptom

issue.reason: Note added that the procedure assumes collection at the gate and that a second offload path will be cross-referenced when it is defined.

The most common cause is not a recording fault at all: the on-board store has filled and overwritten the oldest closed records before anyone connected to collect them. A genuine recording fault shows a gap that is not aligned with the store capacity. Every step below assumes that the records leave the aircraft one way, through a technician with a portable loader at the gate, and that the store fill level therefore tells the whole story. That assumption is about to stop holding: an automatic ground offload path is in pre-analysis, and on an aircraft carrying it a record can be absent from the ground system while it was collected perfectly well, or present although nobody connected to the aircraft. Until that change is defined, do not extend the reasoning here to an aircraft that carries a second path.

In that case record the shortfall and raise the collection interval or the store capacity with the operator's engineering department. 5. If the missing records are inside the retention window, read the record sequence numbers and identify whether the gap is contiguous. 6. A contiguous gap that starts at a power cycle points at an interrupted write rather than at a failed collection. 7. Check the maintenance interface unit for reported write errors and read its fault log. 8. Run the built-in test load and record the result. 9. If the built-in test fails, replace the data server module and repeat the store integrity check. 10. If the built-in test passes and the gap persists on the next rotation, replace the maintenance interface unit.
sections.dispatch_note: There is no dispatch consequence. The condition monitoring function is not required for dispatch and no minimum equipment list item applies, but a persistent recording fault should be cleared before the aircraft next leaves its main base. When the automatic offload path is defined, a cross-reference to its own checks is added at step 2 of the isolation procedure; the branch is deliberately left unwritten here rather than guessed at.
